articles.title: ‘Cracking auction, Gromit!’ Original Aardman puppets go under the hammer
articles.summary: Wallace and Gromit stop-motion models and other beloved creations raise money to train new generations of animators. Wallace’s reaction as the auction got into full swing might have been a trademark “good grief!” – and the enthusiasm of some of the bidding could have caused even the phlegmatic…
body: Fans of Wallace and Gromit and other beloved creations of Aardman Animations seized the chance to grab souvenirs when more than 200 pieces – including Wallace, Gromit, Shaun the Sheep and Chicken Run puppets from Aardman productions – went under the hammer on Thursday.
Sought-after items included Wallace and Gromit stop-motion models from the Bristol studio’s hugely popular 2024 film Vengeance Most Fowl.

Lot 216, for example, was Wallace in his traditional outfit of a knitted green tank top, red tie and brown trousers. The catalogue said he was in “smashing condition”, and gave details of his construction: “Wallace’s head is moulded from clay; while his body is made of silicone to facilitate smooth repositioning by the animators.

“He has a skeleton, just like every salt-of-the-earth lad, it’s just that his happens to be made of metal. His teeth, shirt collar, tie, pen, and pencil are fast-cast resin and his eyes are plastic.” It sold for an eye-popping £50,400.
points: Wallace and Gromit stop-motion models and other beloved creations raise money to train new generations of animators.

articles.title: Aamir Khan to Receive Screen Icon Award as Singapore Film Festival Opens With Hur Jin-ho’s ‘The Assassin(s)’
articles.summary: The Singapore International Film Festival (SGIFF) will present its Screen Icon Award to Indian actor, director and producer Aamir Khan at its 37th edition, with a 25th-anniversary Special Presentation screening of “Lagaan: Once Upon a Time in India” alongside director Ashutosh Gowariker.
body: SGIFF executive director Jeremy Chua said the edition brings some of the most respected talents and consequential work being made across Asia to Singapore. “Around it, we have also reconsidered how audiences encounter a festival with new presentation formats and points of entry, a ticketing platform that is markedly more intuitive, an industry programme expanded into a resource centre for artists, technicians and storytellers at every stage of practice, and a new free-to-attend section at the intersection of creativity and technology, attending to the forms storytelling will take next,” Chua said.

SGIFF’s “In Conversation With” dialogue series will also feature Shim Eun-kyung, filmmaker Peter Chan Ho-sun and Hong Kong actor Anthony Wong, who will take part in a post-screening dialogue tied to his first acting role in “My Name Ain’t Suzie.” Korean New Wave director Yim Soon-rye will serve as jury head of the Asian Feature Film Competition, while Fukada Koji, director of “Nagi Notes,” cinematographers Ashizawa Akiko and Tom Harari, and director Jacob Cheung will also take part in the festival.

articles.title: The Horror Show Launches at Academy Museum: Costumes and Props From ‘Halloween,’ ‘Saw,’ ‘Poltergeist’ and More
articles.summary: Just in time for the scariest season, the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures in Los Angeles is unveiling The Horror Show, a major survey of costumes, props, drawings, posters and other artifacts from the most iconic horror films throughout the history of cinema. The exhibit opens Saturday.
body: From Bela Lugosi’s original cape from the 1931 “Dracula” to Aunt Gladys’ pantsuit from “Weapons,” the exhibit showcases classic and lesser-known films from every era. Beloved characters like Freddy Krueger, Michael Myers and Chucky are represented along with more recent titles such as “Sinners,” “Get Out,” “Midsommar” and “The Babadook.”

“Many different types of films can be considered horror filmmaking, from vampires to slashers to thrillers,” said Academy museum director Amy Homma as she introduced the exhibit Thursday. “Horror has its own filmic history, it’s own origins through literature, culture and art and its own lineage.”

“The Horror Show revolves around a simple question: Why do horror films mean so much to so many people?” said the exhibit’s curator Jessica Niebel. “Horror reflects the anxieties of its time, but it also gives us a safe space to confront those anxieties, to look at the things that frighten us and that we desire.”

articles.title: AI Robots Dance in the Rain as Pingyao Film Festival Turns 10, Honors Ann Hui
articles.summary: The 10th Pingyao Crouching Tiger Hidden Dragon International Film Festival opened on Sept. 24 with an AI robot dance by Unitree, a tribute to four late friends of the festival and the East-West Award for Hong Kong director Ann Hui.
body: Festival founder Jia Zhangke recalled that a soft drizzle had also fallen on the same stage during Pingyao’s very first edition. He thanked the festival team, press and audiences, and his fellow filmmakers in particular.

“I remember one year we hosted the Pingyao Film Festival during a heavy snowfall. Spring Festival was right around the corner and we were so worried that no audience or guests would show up,” Jia said. “Yet that year, so many people who work in the film industry drove through the heavy snow from hundreds, even thousands of kilometers away. In that moment, I felt the snow was burning, fueled by the warmth and support you brought to us.”

Jia said he hoped the festival would carry on for a few more decades. “When I get old enough, I will return simply as a filmgoer, sitting down in the audience, watching a movie right here at the Platform,” he said.

articles.title: Media outlets banned by Trump denied access to White House dinner despite judge's order
articles.summary: CNN and MS NOW said reporters were denied access to covering White House arrivals for a state dinner, despite a judge ruling their passes must be restored.
body: CNN and MS NOW reporters say they have been denied entry to cover a White House state dinner despite a judge ruling their access to the grounds must be restored.

A federal judge said in an overnight ruling that the White House ban on three outlets - CNN and MS NOW and Politico - was likely unconstitutional and that the administration must allow them access, for now. Trump barred them last week, accusing them of "fake news".
Journalists with the three outlets were allowed back in on Thursday morning.
Then in the evening, a CNN reporter and a producer and an MS NOW reporter said that they were denied entry to cover the guests arriving for a state dinner for Chinese leader Xi Jinping.

How often do you get asked to recite that WH Auden poem from Four Weddings and a Funeral, and can you do it from memory right now?
body: In Steve Coogan ’s Paul Calf’s Video Diary, your character praises Orson Welles’ The Trial for its “tremendous energy”, while Paul says he would “rather watch Dave Lee Travis playing Macbeth”. What’s your actual opinion of The Trial [by Franz Kafka]? AdrianH1 God, it’s a long time since I’ve read that. I read a lot of those books in my younger days, but probably, like a lot of people, even those who are graduates of English literature, I’d be hard pushed these days to tell you what it was about, other than the persecution of some minor character.

As a popular jobbing actor, you have a massive list of credits. Has anyone ever come up to you to express their appreciation for a certain role and you had no idea what they were on about? Kevcoe No. It’s always heartwarming when somebody comes up and offers their congratulations on something a little bit lower down the pecking order. Fortunately, people rarely ever come up to tell me that they thought I was shit in something. I quite often get Paul Calf’s Video Diary, and that Macbeth line. To be frank, I can’t quite remember the context.

articles.title: Catherine Zeta-Jones bases new role on funny Welsh people she knows
articles.summary: Zeta-Jones plays Jackie Price, a former cocaine dealer who is targeted by assassins, in Kill Jackie.
body: Actor Catherine Zeta-Jones says she based her performance in the new series Kill Jackie on people she knows in Wales.
The Mumbles star plays Jackie Price, a former cocaine dealer who is being targeted by hitmen, in a new series for Prime.
It is the first time she has played a role using her Swansea accent and the first time she has filmed a drama in Wales.
"I played on people I know in Wales, people who are comedic and the accent makes it funny and real and true, but the character comes from a tough side of Swansea, which we do have as well," she said.

articles.title: Global release announced for acclaimed Gaza documentary NAZA
articles.summary: Theatrical rollout across 56 territories planned for documentary about Israel’s mass killing of civilians in Gaza before film will stream on Guardian website. NAZA, the award-winning documentary from Israeli film-makers Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, is set to be released in cinemas in more than 50…
body: The film, which the Guardian produced, premiered at the Venice film festival earlier this month, where it was met with a 25-minute standing ovation – a festival record. The documentary went on to win the special jury prize.

After screenings in Bologna and at the San Sebastián film festival, the film will receive its North American premiere on Saturday at the New York film festival before opening four days later at the IFC Center in New York City. On 9 October it will expand to Los Angeles and other key US cities before a national rollout.

A theatrical release in partnership with MK2 Films is also planned in 55 other territories, including the UK, Australia, New Zealand, Japan, Canada, Hong Kong, Brazil, Turkey, Thailand, France, Spain, Germany, Turkey, Central America and the Middle East.
After its run in cinemas, the film will stream in late November on the Guardian’s website, for free, as part of the news organisation’s commitment to the dissemination of independent journalism.

articles.title: Inside the Hollywood Home Studio That’s Birthed Several Pop Hits
articles.summary: Music producer Leland speaks with The Hollywood Reporter about his Hollywood home studio, his collaborator Troye Sivan's new album and making queer art.
body: Situated in the hills of Studio City sits a home studio that’s birthed a slew of popular songs.

“The first session I did here was with MUNA in 2019,” says Leland. The 39-year-old producer owns that home studio. It’s first iteration was situated inside the main house on his property and has since expanded into its own little oasis.

The actual studio only accounts for, at times, 50 percent of where the creativity’s happening when artist comes to Leland’s place. “The writing doesn’t have to happen in the studio. The recording can happen in the studio,” the producer explains. “I feel like a lot of it is just sitting out here having conversations.”

An artist might be staying in the cottage on the property while they’re there working. “They can just walk down to the studio, which has been really nice,” says Leland. The Shards star Hayes Warner, another collaborator of Leland’s, stayed in his cottage while she was filming the Ryan Murphy show. Leland wrote music for the series, which is set to release a soundtrack next month.
